content: If someone has overdosed and is experiencing severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. If the situation is less urgent, contact a poison control center right away. In the United States, you can call 1-800-222-1222, and in Canada, you can call 1-844-764-7669. This medication has been prescribed specifically for your current condition. Laboratory or medical tests, such as urine cultures, may be conducted while you are taking this medication to monitor its effectiveness. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This medication is an antibiotic used to treat bladder infections, such as acute cystitis or lower urinary tract infections, in women. It works by inhibiting the growth of bacteria. However, it is only effective against bacterial infections and will not work for viral infections like the common cold or flu. Before taking this medication, read the patient information leaflet provided by your pharmacist. Take the medication by mouth as directed by your doctor, usually as a single dose of one packet (sachet). Mix the contents of the packet with half a glass (4 ounces or 120 milliliters) of cold water and stir until dissolved. Do not use warm or hot water. Your symptoms should improve within 2 to 3 days. Common side effects may include diarrhea, nausea, headache, vaginal discomfort, or dizziness. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Rarely, this medication may cause a severe intestinal condition due to a bacteria called Clostridium difficile (C. diff), which can occur during treatment or weeks to months after treatment has stopped. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. Before taking this medication, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. If you develop symptoms of a kidney infection, such as pain in your side or lower back, fever, or chills, contact your doctor immediately. This medication may cause dizziness. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can increase this effect. Avoid driving, using machinery, or performing tasks that require alertness until you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages. This product may contain sugar and/or aspartame, so caution is advised if you have diabetes, phenylketonuria (PKU), or any other condition requiring you to limit or avoid these substances in your diet. Fosfomycin may reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed. It passes into breast milk in small amounts but is unlikely to harm a nursing infant. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk for serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. If someone has overdosed and is experiencing severe symptoms such as passing out or trouble breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center. In the U.S., call 1-800-222-1222, and in Canada, call 1-844-764-7669. This medication has been prescribed for your current condition only. Laboratory and/or medical tests, such as urine cultures, may be conducted while you are taking this medication to monitor its effectiveness. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed.
